correctness.rationale: All eight L=3 stationary weights are explicit positive polynomials over a common positive cubic; direct substitution proves stationarity and normalization for all r>=0. Moments yield the exact quartic. Descartes two-change upper bound and rational signs at r=0,1/4,1 force exactly two simple positive roots and strict interval signs. The general L=2 four-state generator gives affine covariance numerator, proving sharp minimal length. Open rate neighbourhood follows continuity and strict rational signs. The standalone public checker reconstructs both generators and passes 24 exact identities and sign assertions; numerical roots are supplementary, not the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating original model treats nearest-neighbour covariance as a diagnostic for interacting local resetting but chiefly uses mean-field/Monte Carlo, potentially hiding exact small-system effects. An analytically exact negative-positive-negative downstream correlation transition at the minimal admissible length, separated from the all-positive-rate two-site impossibility and stable to perturbations of the injection/extraction rates, is a physically meaningful structural finite-size boundary. This is not merely an unmotivated exact fraction or normalization check: it identifies the earliest system size at which a two-window correlation sign response occurs and shows it is not a singular parameter accident. No thermodynamic phase-transition claim is made.
